newsitem.title: UK: Ship's crew not paid for eight months - ITF claims.
newsitem.headline: Ship's crew not paid for eight months - ITF claims.

text.p: The Russian and Ukranian crew of a Panamanian-registered ship have not been paid wages for eight months, International Transport Workers Federation claimed Wednesday.
ITF said the 11 crew of the 2,068gt City of Athens refused to discharge a cargo of pipes in protest as part of the union's European week of action against flags of convenience.
The crew were threatened with legal action if they continued to prevent unloading at the Italian port of Choggia and agreed to open the hatches, the ITF said.
But they rejected an offered part-payment of $25,000 as it was only a third of the $74,000 owed, the union added.
ITF said it has engaged lawyers in Venice and is attempting to arrest the ship.

ITF also said a second ship, the 24,000 dwt Maltese flag bulk carrier Irina, is under threat of boycott at the Norwegian port of Porsgrunn. Negotiations were taking place to secure an ITF agreement for the Romanian crew.

The 42,000dwt bulk carrier Blue L remained under boycott at Porsgrunn over payment of back wages, it added. The ship has been held up since Monday. - Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
